conventions.convention: Order orientation and preservation bounds: q ≤ p means q is stronger; a forcing preorder need not be antisymmetric; κ-closure quantifies over descending sequences of length γ < κ, κ-distributivity over fewer than κ dense open sets, and κ-cc over antichains of cardinality below κ, so ccc is ℵ₁-cc and 'countably closed' means ℵ₁-closed, never ω-closed.
Nice names have the form ẋ = {⟨ǎ,p⟩ : a ∈ A, p ∈ A_a} with each A_a an antichain; empty antichains are allowed, A = ∅ gives the empty name, and niceness alone asserts nothing about arbitrary names.

Cohen/collapse/Lévy orders are reverse-inclusion partial-function orders: Add(κ,λ) = Fn(λ×κ,2,<κ), Col(κ,λ) = Fn(κ,λ,<κ) for infinite κ ≤ λ, and Lv(θ) consists of finite p with dom p ⊆ θ×ω and p(α,n) < α; the empty function is the largest condition.

Two-step iterations are formed inside the bounded set carrier R of P-names whose domains lie in the closure of dom(Q̇) under immediate subnames, with (p,q̇) ≤ (p',q̇') iff p ≤_P p' and p ⊩ q̇ ≤_Q̇ q̇'; AC makes this dense-equivalent to the unrestricted local-name convention, and the definition claims no factorization or chain condition.

Finite support of a limit-stage condition is {α < γ : p↾α ⊬ p(α) = 1̇_α} (forced-equal-to-top coordinates count as outside the support), conditions are coherent across all coordinates, and the order is coordinatewise in the forcing sense, p ≤ q iff p↾α ⊩ p(α) ≤ q(α) for every α.
MA(κ) concerns families of at most κ dense subsets of a nonempty ccc order, and MA is the scheme MA(κ) for every infinite κ < 2^{ℵ₀}; the inequality is strict and MA(2^{ℵ₀}) is not included.
Stopping times are maps τ: Ω → ℕ₀ ∪ {∞} with {τ ≤ n} ∈ F_n for every n, literally (no completion, no null-set modification); bounded (τ ≤ N a.s.) is strictly stronger than finite (P(τ < ∞) = 1).
F_τ = {A ∈ F : A ∩ {τ ≤ n} ∈ F_n for every n}, with τ allowed to equal ∞ and membership read literally; for deterministic τ = n this is exactly F_n.

X_τ = Σ_{k≥0} X_k 1_{τ=k} + x_∞ 1_{τ=∞} for a fixed real cemetery value x_∞; an actual terminal variable replaces x_∞ only when separately supplied and stated, and the stopped process X_{n∧τ} never evaluates the cemetery value.
Upcrossing counts use non-strict levels: x_{s_i} ≤ a and x_{t_i} ≥ b along 0 ≤ s_1 < t_1 < ... < s_k < t_k ≤ N, the empty tuple contributes 0, and U_∞ = sup_N U_N.
Reverse filtrations decrease (G_0 ⊇ G_1 ⊇ ...), G_∞ = ∩_n G_n, and a reverse martingale satisfies E[X_m|G_n] = X_n for m ≤ n, with the adjacent identities alone sufficient.

Martingale-difference arrays are indexed by n,k ≥ 1 with F_{n,k} increasing in k, Z_{n,k} ∈ L², F_{n,k}-measurable and conditionally centered; the variance clock is Γ_{n,m} = Σ_{k≤m} E[Z²_{n,k}|F_{n,k-1}], and finite rows are padded by Z_{n,k} = 0 with the filtration held fixed.

Symmetric forcing systems: HS names are those whose stabilizer lies in the normal filter and all of whose subnames are HS, and N = HS_F^{G_0} for a ground-model generic G_0 that is not the automorphism group G; π acts on names by πẋ = {⟨πp,πẏ⟩ : ⟨p,ẏ⟩ ∈ ẋ}, which fixes check names and preserves rank.

Basic Cohen system: P = Add(ω,ω) of finite partial maps ω×ω → 2, a finite permutation π of ω acting by (πp)(πn,m) = p(n,m), filter generated by fix(E) for finite E ⊆ ω, with ȧ_n = {⟨p,m̌⟩ : p(n,m)=1} and Ȧ = {⟨1_P,ȧ_n⟩ : n ∈ ω}.

Atom-free socks system: coordinate (n,i,j) adds a real r_{n,i,j}, R_{n,i} = {r_{n,i,j} : j}, P_n = {R_{n,0},R_{n,1}}; automorphisms preserve n, may swap the two i-blocks independently for each n and permute j-coordinates within blocks, and the normal filter is generated by finite pointwise coordinate stabilizers, so symmetric objects are exactly the finitely supported ones.

ZFA: atoms have no members but are not the empty set, Extensionality is restricted to non-atoms, V_0(A) = A, V_{α+1}(A) = V_α(A) ∪ P(V_α(A)); pure means the transitive closure contains no atom, and the pure kernel is a transitive ZF model, choice-free, to which ambient AC restricts.

Permutation supports: symmetric means the stabilizer lies in the normal filter F, and a finite E supports x when fix_G(E) ⊆ sym_G(x); the Fraenkel and Mostowski models use the filter generated by the finite-support subgroups, so there symmetric = finitely supported, and hereditary symmetry (all members of the transitive closure symmetric) is required for model membership.

Boundable means ∃x̄ φ(x̄) with a fixed finite m such that every quantifier of φ is bounded by P^m(∪x̄) (lower iterates allowed), so truth is determined by that bounded membership structure; full AC and arbitrary sentences are not boundable.

The Jech–Sochor first embedding is stated for every ordinal α of M and yields a membership isomorphism P^α(A)^V ≅ P^α(A*)^W respecting all lower iterates; ambient ZFA+AC is the only choice hypothesis and none is claimed inside V or W.

load_bearing.statement: The order is κ-closed if every descending sequence of length γ < κ has a common lower bound, κ-distributive if the intersection of every family of fewer than κ dense open subsets of P is dense, and κ-cc if every antichain has cardinality below κ; ccc is ℵ₁-cc and countably closed means ℵ₁-closed.

The two-step iteration P*Q̇ is the set of pairs (p,q̇) ∈ P×R with p ⊩ q̇ ∈ Q̇, ordered by (p,q̇) ≤ (p',q̇') iff p ≤_P p' and p ⊩ q̇ ≤_Q̇ q̇'; under AC the bounded-carrier convention is dense-equivalent to the unrestricted local-name convention, and the definition makes no generic-factorization or chain-condition assertion.

Successor stages are P_{α+1} = P_α*Q̇_α with largest condition (1_{P_α},1̇_α); at a limit γ a condition is a coherent function on γ with finite support {α < γ : p↾α ⊬ p(α) = 1̇_α} and the order is coordinatewise in the forcing sense.

Every P-name forced to be a subset of a ground-model set A is forced equal to a nice name; if P is ccc with |P| = μ infinite and |A| = λ then there are at most (μ^{ℵ₀})^λ nice names for subsets of A, in particular at most μ^{ℵ₀} nice names for reals.
For infinite regular κ and λ > 0, Add(κ,λ) is κ-closed and has (2^{<κ})^+-cc; hence Add(ω,λ) is ccc, and if 2^{<κ} = κ then Add(κ,λ) has κ^+-cc.
In ZFC, if every P_α forces Q̇_α ccc, then every P_β of the finite-support iteration is ccc.

MA(κ) says that whenever P is a nonempty ccc forcing preorder and D is a family of at most κ dense subsets of P, there is a filter meeting every member of D; MA is the scheme MA(κ) for every infinite κ < 2^{ℵ₀}, with strict inequality.
For a transitive ZF ground model M, a symmetric system and an M-generic G_0, N = HS_F^{G_0} is a transitive ZF model with M ⊆ N ⊆ M[G_0]; no Choice hypothesis is required.
For a transitive ZFA model M and a normal permutation system (A,G,F), HS_F^M is a transitive ZFA model with the same atoms and pure kernel; even if M satisfies AC, HS_F^M need not.

For every ordinal α of M there is a symmetric ZF extension W of the pure kernel K and A* ∈ W such that P^α(A)^V and P^α(A*)^W are membership-isomorphic, respecting all lower iterates; the ambient AC supplies only cardinal comparison and a pure coordinate copy of A.
Every map from ω into A in the basic Cohen model has finite range; therefore no injection ω → A, no countably infinite subset, and no enumeration of A exists in that model.
Assume AC. If X is a submartingale with C := sup_n E[X_n^+] < ∞, then there is an integrable finite random variable X_∞ with X_n → X_∞ almost surely.

Assume AC. For a martingale M the following are equivalent: (1) {M_n} is uniformly integrable; (2) M_n converges in L¹ to some M_∞; (3) M_n = E[X|F_n] a.s. for some X ∈ L¹; and one may take X = M_∞, with almost-sure convergence additionally.

Assume AC. If M is a martingale and σ ≤ τ are stopping times bounded by a deterministic N, then E[M_τ|F_σ] = M_σ a.s., so E M_τ = E M_σ; for submartingales the conditional and expectation inequalities point upward and for supermartingales downward.
For τ: Ω → ℕ₀ ∪ {∞} the conditions {τ ≤ n} ∈ F_n, {τ = n} ∈ F_n and {τ > n} ∈ F_n for all n are equivalent, and then {τ ≥ n} ∈ F_{n-1} for n ≥ 1.
Assume AC. If (F_n) is increasing with F_∞ = σ(∪_n F_n) and X ∈ L¹, then E[X|F_n] → E[X|F_∞] almost surely and in L¹.

concerns.concern: Step 1.2 says 'For a condition U use F2 to choose a finite union W ⊆ U of rational intervals with m(U∖W) < (ε-m(U))/2', citing [F2] lem-elementary-sets-admit-compact-inner-and-open-outer-approximations, and then counts 'Only countably many sets W occur'. The cited lemma supplies inner approximation by elementary sets with arbitrary real endpoints and says nothing about rational endpoints, so the citation is stronger than its source and the countability claim is not licensed as written. The missing fact is closable from the cited lemma plus density of the rational intervals (U is a countable union of rational subintervals, and continuity from below of the measure gives a finite subunion W ⊆ U with the required slack), but the proof as written has to be repaired by the reader before the σ-centeredness argument is valid.

Step 1.1 (limit of countable cofinality) argues: uncountably many members of an alleged ω₁-antichain have supports below one stage α, 'their restrictions cannot all be pairwise incompatible there by induction, and compatible restrictions amalgamate their disjoint tails using F2'. Compatibility of restrictions does not imply amalgamation for arbitrary P_β-conditions — in a two-step P_α*Q̇, conditions with compatible first coordinates and forced-incompatible second coordinates have no common extension — so the stated reason is a non-sequitur as written. The argument is correct only on the reading that the subfamily in question has support below α, so its members already are P_α-conditions with top tails; a reader must supply that reading (the uncountable-cofinality case 2.1 uses the correct disjoint-petal argument).

Step 1.1's 'otherwise choose for each α an extension q_α ≤ p_α incompatible with a tail, and recursively select an uncountable subsequence of the q_α that is pairwise incompatible, contradicting ccc' is compressed to the point that the selection is not justified: each q_α is only incompatible with a tail of the p_α's, so pairwise incompatibility of the selected q_α's requires the recursion to choose each next index above all previously produced tail-bounds, and it requires the set of α at which p_α admits such an extension to be unbounded (otherwise a single p_* already works). The conclusion (MA(ℵ₁) ⇒ every ccc order is Knaster ⇒ ccc products) is correct once that reading is supplied.

This is a meta-mathematical claim that PA proves totality and checker acceptance for a large emitted proof construction. The proof describes the reflection/Skolem-hull/collapse block, the tagged ZFA+AC interpretation, the forcing/symmetry blocks and the two interpretation passes at the level of fixed templates, and asserts the checker invariant and PA induction rather than discharging them block by block; I could not verify the coding-level details in a reading pass, so I record residual uncertainty rather than a located defect (the statement itself is explicitly hedged to fixed certified presentations and disclaims full-ZFC CTM inferences). The same character applies to the sibling compilers lem-formal-cohen-forcing-verification-compiler, lem-formal-ma-iteration-verification-compiler and lem-basic-cohen-symmetric-construction-is-uniformly-formalizable, whose interfaces with lem-forcing-transfer-for-finite-zfc-fragments, thm-formal-consistency-transfer-by-forcing and thm-formal-relative-consistency-from-verified-proof-reduction I checked and found faithful.

The recursion in step 1.2 is worded ambiguously: 'Recursively choose x_{ξ_μ} for μ < θ so that x_{ξ_μ}(i_0) exceeds α_0 and every element of the earlier chosen sets.' For the subsequent claim ('distinct chosen sets meet only below α_0' and hence intersection r) what is needed is that the i_0-th point of each new set exceeds α_0 and also exceeds every element of all earlier chosen sets; with that reading the argument is correct (elements of an earlier set above α_0 are ≥ its i_0-th point, and the later i_0-th point sits above all of them), and the choice is possible because the i_0-th coordinates are unbounded in θ. Only the wording of the requirement is at issue.
